newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Rally takes Bucharest share prices up.
newsitem.headline: Rally takes Bucharest share prices up.

text.p: The Bucharest bourse pursued a week-long rally on Friday, with more than three in five of its listings posting gains, and traders predicted further rises next week.
"Buying pressure continued today, stronger on the lower tier, and we expect it stay in the market early next week too," said a trader.

Two independent market indices, the VAB and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, rose by 3.29 and 3.31 percent respectively from Thursday. The other unofficial index, the BIG, was not available.
A bourse closing report showed the average prices of 31 stocks climbed and of nine slipped. Four companies had no deal and two were suspended.
Volume grew to 5.4 million shares from 2.7 million and turnover doubled to 26.9 billion lei.
"Activity was busier than usual on the second tier and this was nice for a change. For the first time in weeks, we had only four stocks with no deal rather than at least seven," a broker said.
But trading focused on the blue chips, with four of the seven traded stocks closing higher. Arctic refrigerator maker remained suspended pending privatisation.

Chemical plants Oltchim and Sofert ended 50 and 300 lei stronger respectively at 5,300 and 36,500. Antibiotice pharmaceuticals and Compa vehicle parts maker also picked up, rising 500 and 200 lei to 9,200 and 2,900.
Pharmaceuticals company Terapia and Policolor dye maker were unchanged at 6,450 and 12,500.
Armatura industrial fittings maker and carbide producer Carbid-Fox remained the most heavily traded stocks on the second tier. Both firmed, gaining 300 and 350 lei to 7,200 and 7,350.
The VAB index is displayed on VANGUARD.
